problems.issue: No way to attach the payload at the tip. DESIGN.md and requirement arm_torque are built around a 50 g test weight at arm.tip (100 mm from the pivot), but arm.py ends in a solid rounded tip with no hole or hook. The user would have to tape the weight on somewhere near the end, so the lever arm (and the torque being tested) is not repeatable.
problems.fix: In arm.py cut a vertical clearance hole on the arm.tip axis at (0, -arm_len): M3 clearance (3.5 mm, leaving about 5.2 mm of wall each side in the 14 mm arm) or M4 (4.5 mm). An M3 bolt with stacked nuts or washers, or a hanging hook, then puts the 50 g exactly at 100 mm. Add a line to the DESIGN.md assembly order saying how the test mass is made and hung.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew any part (its own part was not touched)

problems.issue: The servo tab hole pattern (49.5 x 10 mm, 4.2 mm holes) is marked UNVERIFIED in the catalog and REFERENCES.md (it is copied from a DS3218 drawing), yet it is locked into heat-set inserts. An M3 screw in a 4.2 mm tab hole can only shift about 0.6 mm, so if the real servo uses the 48 mm Futaba-style spacing the screws will not start.
problems.fix: Before printing the bracket, caliper-measure the actual MG996R's tab hole centres and record the verified value with a source in catalog/hardware.json. Or first print a 2 mm-thick test plate with just the window and the 4 holes (about 10 minutes) and test-fit the servo.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: The tab screws are sized for bare tabs: tab_t 2.5 mm plus M3x8 gives 5.5 mm of thread in the insert. The MG996R ships with rubber grommets and brass eyelets, which the catalog's 4.2 mm hole note anticipates. With those fitted, the tab stack is roughly twice as thick and the screw grips only a couple of threads. Without grommets, a 5.5 mm socket head rests on just a 0.65 mm ring of plastic tab around the 4.2 mm hole.
problems.fix: In DESIGN.md assembly step 3, state 'leave the rubber grommets out; fit an M3 washer under each screw head' and add 4x M3 washers to the BOM. Alternatively, size the screws for the grommet stack and declare that grip.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: Only 2.1 mm of plastic separates each tab-screw insert hole from the servo window: the hole edge is at x = 22.75 mm and the window edge at x = 20.65 mm. That meets the catalog minimum (1.6 mm) but not the 2.4 mm in ENGINEERING section 5. Melting an insert this close to a free edge in PETG tends to bulge the thin web into a window that has only 0.3 mm of clearance per side, which can stop the servo body from passing.
problems.fix: Cut the window to the body width only between the tab hole rows. Or reduce the window's length clearance to 0.4 mm and add 0.5 mm local relief behind each insert, giving at least 2.4 mm of web. At minimum, melt the inserts with the servo out and check the window afterwards.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: When printed on its back, the foot stands vertical, so the 4 M3 clearance holes in the foot print as horizontal holes. Their tops will sag, contrary to ENGINEERING section 4.
problems.fix: Make these foot holes teardrop-shaped, with the point toward the print +Z, or open them to 3.7 mm.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: Inside corners on the load path have no fillets, contrary to ENGINEERING section 5: where the gussets meet the wall and the foot, and the four corners of the servo window, which carry the tab-screw couple.
problems.fix: Add r>=1 mm fillets at the gusset roots. For the window, use r=1 mm corner fillets (the servo case corners are radiused) or dog-bone reliefs.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: The bracket_fea load case understates the load and uses a lower safety factor than the rules require. Each +/-18.6 N load is spread over a box from x=1 to x=30.75 mm, so its centroid is about 15.9 mm from the axis rather than at the 24.75 mm screw position. The applied moment is about 590 N*mm, roughly 64% of the 922 N*mm stall moment. The case also uses SF 2.0 against layer-direction strength, while ENGINEERING section 3 asks for SF 3.0 across layers. The current margin is about 30x, so the verdict does not change, but the check would under-report on larger parameter values.
problems.fix: Apply each force on a small box (about 3 mm) centred on the tab-screw insert positions (x = +/-servo_hx/2, z = pivot_h +/- 5), and set sf: 3.0.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: ENGINEERING section 8 calls for a second support for the servo output when the link is longer than about 60 mm, and this arm is 100 mm. DESIGN.md does not explain why the rule is not followed here. In practice it is fine: about 0.6 N static radial load on the MG996R's ball-bearing output. But the rules require a written justification.
problems.fix: Add a sizing line to DESIGN.md giving the radial load and overturning moment on the output (static and at full slew) and why the servo's own bearings carry them without a second support.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew any part (its own part was not touched)

problems.issue: The tip hole fixes the earlier major finding: a 3.5 mm hole at (0, -arm_len) with 5.25 mm of wall each side, confirmed in the geometry. The test mass that DESIGN.md and the BOM specify cannot be built, though. A DIN 125 M8 washer (16 OD, 8.4 ID, 1.6 thick) weighs about 1.8 g, so 50 g takes about 27 washers, a stack about 44 mm long. An M3 x 20 through the 6 mm arm with a 2.4 mm nut leaves about 11.6 mm, room for only about 13 g. M8 washers on a 3 mm shank also sit up to 2.7 mm off-centre, which moves the load point and defeats the reason for the hole.
problems.fix: Change the BOM line and assembly step 7 to something that works. For example, hang a 50 g calibration weight or fishing sinker from the hole on a wire loop. Or use M3 x 50 + nut with a slug of known mass. Or use an M8 x 30 bolt + 2 nuts (about 50 g) hung on an S-hook through the hole. Then weigh the actual mass on a kitchen scale and note it.

problems.issue: The tab screws are now thread-forming M3 screws in 2.72 mm pilot holes, confirmed 7.2 mm deep. That removes the thin-web problem: the pilot-hole edge is at x = 23.39 and the window at 20.65, a 2.74 mm web. Also, iface.screw_spec always uses the PLA pilot value (2.72). The catalog note for fdm_holes.M3 gives 2.60 for PETG, and this part is PETG, so each screw gets less thread engagement than intended.

problems.issue: The arm carries the payload but has no fea_static requirement, which ENGINEERING section 3b asks of every structural part. A hand check shows a large margin: the in-plane section modulus is 6 x 14^2 / 6 = 196 mm^3, giving 0.27 MPa under gravity and about 4.7 MPa if the servo stalls against a blocked tip. But the rule asks for the proof, plus a deflection limit (1% of length).
problems.fix: Add an fea_static requirement for the arm: fixed at the horn bolt circle, a stall-torque-equivalent force (922 N*mm / 100 mm = 9.2 N) at arm.tip, XY strength, SF 2, max_disp_mm 1.0.
problems.resolved_how: no part was redrawn; closed by the next review/check result

problems.issue: The keyhole slots make the washers load-bearing, not optional. A DIN 125 M3 washer (7 mm OD) centred on a hole at x = 24.75 reaches x = 28.25, which is 1.25 mm past the 54 mm tab end, so it bears on a partial ring, roughly 1.25 mm strips on each side of the slot. That is adequate for the in-plane stall couple: the +/-18.6 N acts in Z, across the slots, which open along X. But the washer is the only thing stopping the head from pulling into the slot. The fastener check also counts a 2.5 mm grip without the 0.5 mm washer, so engagement is really 5.0 mm in the 7.2 mm pilot (minimum 4.5), not 5.5.
problems.fix: Leave the geometry as it is. In DESIGN.md assembly step 3 say 'washers are required (the tab holes are slots open to the end)' and note that M3 x 8 gives 5.0 mm of thread with the washer. If the grommets are ever left in, the screws must go to M3 x 12.

problems.issue: DESIGN.md 'Load -> section' says the bracket's moment peaks at 'wall bending at its root over the foot'. That is wrong for the design load case. The stall couple (+/-18.6 N along Z at the tab pilots) bends the 88 mm wall IN its own plane, and the FEA puts the peaks at the servo-window corners (bracket hot zone [-20.8, 7.8, 69.7]) and in the foot by the outer screws (peak 1.36 MPa at [38.4, 15.4, 5.0]). The wall root over the foot is the stress map's coldest region (cold zones [-36.2, 7.8, 8.0], [-20.8, 7.8, 8.0], [25.5, 7.8, 8.0], 0-1 % use). The section reasoning in the record therefore does
problems.fix: Rewrite the bracket row: the peak is where the window interrupts the wall between the pilot pairs and the foot, and in the foot plate between the wall and the outer screws. Say the wall root and the gussets are there for out-of-plane stiffness (servo mass and the swinging arm), which no FEA case loads.

problems.issue: The overbuilt justification has the right conclusion but wrong support. (a) It says 'the 80 mm wall width'; wall_w is 88 mm (report params). (c) 'the stand check wants the mass low' argues for the foot and base, not for the 88 x 93 x 8 wall: most of the wall's mass is above the pivot line's midpoint and raises the CG, and `stand` has 37.1 deg against a 15 deg requirement. (d) The 7.2 mm pilot depth sets 8 mm only at the four pilot bosses, not across the whole slab. The 4 % figure itself is correct (s
problems.fix: Correct 80 to 88 mm. Drop 'the base less' or add a base load case. Justify the wall with stiffness the FEA does not load (out-of-plane: the 55 g servo cantilevered behind the wall, arm inertia on fast swings; deflection now 0.021 mm) plus print simplicity (one flat bed face that the tabs seat on). Optional ~15 g saving: a 2-3 mm pocket in the front face below the tie slots, inside an 8 mm frame th

problems.issue: Outside edges are broken only in places, so the edge language claimed in DESIGN.md ('0.6-1.0 mm edge chamfers'; style edge_break 0.8) does not hold on this part. Mesh check of out/parts/bracket.stl: the wall top front edge and the top corners have 1.0 mm chamfers, and the wall's outer vertical edges got r1.5 only because the gusset-root edge filter (|x| = gusset_x + gusset_t/2 = 44) happens to catch them. Still sharp 90 deg: all four gusset hypotenuse edges (~51 mm and ~59 mm each) and the whole perimeter of the foot's front face (85, 88 and 2 x 46 mm). These are the edges a hand grabs. ENGINE
problems.fix: After the cuts, chamfer 0.8 mm on the convex edges of the gusset hypotenuse faces and the foot's front face, leaving the bed face alone. Select them explicitly, not with group_by(Axis.Z)[-1], which picks up only the wall top. Make the wall-side r1.5 deliberate, or say in the code that the gusset-root filter is meant to include it.

problems.issue: Gusset toe kept sharp (sharp_kept at [+/-40, 42.6, 6.0]). The stated reason is true: the hypotenuse rises 43.9 over 35.5 = 51 deg, so the open corner is 129 deg (Kt is small), and the FEA shows the toe in the coldest band. I accept it. But a knife-edge wedge tip is the amateur way to end a gusset: it is the part that chips and the reason OCC cannot fillet it.
problems.fix: Optional: end the gusset with a 1-1.5 mm vertical flat at the toe (polygon vertex at foot_t + 1.5 instead of a point). The toe can then take the standard r1 fillet and sharp_kept becomes empty.

problems.issue: Constant 18 x 6 mm section from hub to tip, although the DESIGN table itself says the moment runs from 0 at the tip to 922 N mm at the hub. Stiffness governs (deflection 0.751 of 1.0 mm, stress 17 % of allowable), and the stress map shows the outer 40 % idle (cold zones at 0.6-2.6 % use). The bending depth is in the right plane (in-plane width, loads along the layers) and the r4 hub blend is right. The bar is acceptable, not derived.
problems.fix: Optional: taper the width from ~22 mm at the hub blend to ~12 mm at the tip (tip boss kept at r6 around the 3.4 mm hole). For a tip load that moves stiffness to the root and should keep deflection at or under 0.75 mm with less tip mass; re-run arm_fea. Also add a 0.4 mm bed-side chamfer so elephant's foot does not lip the edge that rides next to the horn.

problems.issue: A flat slab with holes. Every feature has a purpose (blind M3 inserts with a floor, which I verified by section, 7.6 mm M4 counterbores, r6 corners, 0.8 mm top chamfer), but two purposeful features are missing. Nothing locates the bracket foot: 4 x M3 in 3.4 mm clearance holes is the only registration. And the servo lead and the desk wiring leave the rig with no anchor on the base.
problems.fix: Optional: a 0.5 mm deep pocket or two 1 mm ribs matching the foot outline (0.2 mm clearance per side), so the foot drops in square before the screws go in. Add a cable-tie slot pair or a notch at the base's rear edge for the servo lead.

problems.issue: out/plates/PRINT_SETTINGS.md labels the bracket orientation 'on its front (-Y) face', while DESIGN.md and the part docstring call the same face (part y = 0, the face the tabs seat on) the BACK face. The 3MF carries the correct rotation, but a user re-orienting by hand could flip it, and then the window would need a bridge and the lead-in would end up on the wrong face.
problems.fix: Engine-side: name faces by the part's own docstring or the axis only ('-Y face'), or add a project-level orientation note that the print package quotes.
